key_insight: LGTM (Less Gaussians, Texture More) breaks the resolution bottleneck of feed‑forward Gaussian splatting by predicting compact geometric Gaussians and equipping each with its own texture, so fine detail is handled by textures instead of by exploding primitive counts.
problem_solved: Existing feed‑forward 3D Gaussian Splatting methods require pixel‑aligned primitives, causing primitive count to grow quadratically with output resolution and making high‑resolution synthesis (e.g., 4K) impractical.
method: Predict a compact set of Gaussian primitives that capture coarse geometry (far fewer primitives than pixel‑aligned approaches).
Associate each Gaussian with a per‑primitive texture to encode high‑frequency detail, decoupling appearance detail from geometric density.
Render by feed‑forward textured splatting (with texture sampling/aggregation) to efficiently synthesize high‑resolution outputs such as 4K.
impact: Enables practical, feed‑forward high‑resolution neural rendering (4K) with much lower memory and compute costs, making high‑quality view synthesis and real‑time applications more accessible to practitioners.
visual_elements: Before vs After comparison: dense pixel‑aligned gaussians vs LGTM's sparse textured gaussians (side‑by‑side 4K render).
Pipeline diagram: input -> compact gaussian prediction -> per‑primitive texture assignment -> textured splatting -> 4K output.
Chart of primitive count vs output resolution: quadratic growth (baseline) vs flat/sublinear curve (LGTM).
Icon set: speed (clock), memory (RAM), quality (HD/4K), and scalability (graph arrow).
paper_title: Less Gaussians, Texture More: 4K Feed-Forward Textured Splatting
paper_authors: Yixing Lao, Xuyang Bai, Xiaoyang Wu, Nuoyuan Yan, Zixin Luo
